comment: Hand-written from the @spfn/core 0.3.0-beta.28 state README; the W-cells instead from issue #104 and docs/architecture/state-client-design.md §2-14, not from the README. Rendered by derive-expected-values.py from state_cases.py. docs/architecture/state-client-design.md §3, §4.

cases.name: o1_noEntry_frameApplies
cases.readme: Ordering: no current entry, or `at` newer than the stamp | the ordering stamp advances; applied and notified only when `status`, `value` or `data` differ

cases.name: o2_newerFrame_replacesAndNotifies
cases.readme: Ordering: no current entry, or `at` newer than the stamp | the ordering stamp advances; applied and notified only when `status`, `value` or `data` differ

cases.name: o3_newerSameValue_advancesStampOnly
cases.readme: Ordering: A listener hears it only when `status`, `value` or `data` changed. The `at` of `current()` is the `at` of the read that last changed the value

cases.name: o4_olderFrame_isDropped
cases.readme: Ordering: `at` older than the stamp | dropped

cases.name: o5_equalAtSameValue_changesNothing
cases.readme: Ordering: `at` equal to the stamp | one read stamps one `at`, so this is the same value: applied and notified only when `value` or `data` differ

cases.name: o6_equalAtOtherValue_applies
cases.readme: Ordering: `at` equal to the stamp | one read stamps one `at`, so this is the same value: applied and notified only when `value` or `data` differ

cases.name: o7_dataChange_notifies
cases.readme: Ordering: applied and notified only when `status`, `value` or `data` differ

cases.name: o8_olderThanAdvancedStamp_isDropped
cases.readme: Ordering: a later read that repeats it advances only the stamp, so an older arrival after it is still dropped

cases.name: o9_olderSnapshot_keepsNewerState_appliesOthers
cases.readme: Ordering: a snapshot older than one state's stamp | that state keeps its entry; the others take the snapshot

cases.name: o10_writeAnswer_thenOwnFrame_notifiesOnce
cases.readme: Ordering: a write answer | applied like a frame — its own frame, arriving later with the same `at` and value, changes nothing

cases.name: o11_frameForUnsubscribedKey_isDropped
cases.readme: Ordering: a frame for a key not subscribed here | dropped (the server already filters by the connect query; this is the second guard)

cases.name: o12_atComparedAsUtf8_acrossBoundaries
cases.readme: At: `at` is `new Date().toISOString()`; Ordering: a larger `at` is a later value

cases.name: o13_objectKeyOrder_isNotAChange
cases.readme: Ordering: applied and notified only when `status`, `value` or `data` differ (deep-equal)

cases.name: o14_arrayOrder_isAChange
cases.readme: Ordering: applied and notified only when `status`, `value` or `data` differ (deep-equal)

cases.name: k1_firstKeyedSubscribe_setsQuery
cases.readme: The stream: the connect query is the union of the subscribed keys' fields … A new key value … closes the stream and opens it with the new query

cases.name: k2_sameKeyTwice_keepsQuery
cases.readme: The stream: the connect query is the union of the subscribed keys' fields

cases.name: k3_conflictingKey_latestCarried_shadowReadOnce
cases.readme: The stream: the most recently subscribed key is carried. A key the stream does not carry is read once (`get`) when the stream opens

cases.name: k4_frameForShadowedKey_appliesUnderOrdering
cases.readme: Ordering: a frame for a key not subscribed here | dropped (a subscribed key's frame is applied); The stream: receives no frames until it is carried again

cases.name: k5_lastSubscriberOfKey_leaves_requeries
cases.readme: The stream: or the last subscriber of one leaving, closes the stream and opens it with the new query

cases.name: k8_wrongKeyFields_refusedNamingBothSets
cases.readme: The manifest: a `subscribe` … whose key fields differ from the state's, is refused: the error, naming the state and both sets of fields, goes to `onError`, and the subscription is dropped without reopening the stream

cases.name: k9_unknownId_refused
cases.readme: The manifest: a `subscribe` whose id it does not name … is refused

cases.name: k10_wrongKeyBeforeManifest_waitsThenRefused
cases.readme: The manifest: Until then a `subscribe` waits (it never throws)… Once the manifest is known, a `subscribe` … is refused

cases.name: k11_keylessEntry_ignoresQueryKeys
cases.readme: createStateClient: keyed states under the query's key (a keyless state has no key)

cases.name: k12_seenKey_resubscribe_showsCachedReady
cases.readme: useServerState: a key seen before shows its cached entry as 'ready' until the reopen's frame or snapshot lands (entries are not evicted)

cases.name: k13_keyedEntryWithoutQueryKey_isSkipped
cases.readme: createStateClient (snapshot): Read every state the query names a key for

cases.name: r1_subscriptionRevoked_marksCarriedKey
cases.readme: 'revoked': `subscription.revoked` … the entry of `id` for the key the connection carries … gets `status: 'revoked'`, value kept, listeners notified

cases.name: r2_subscriptionRevoked_leavesShadowedKey
cases.readme: 'revoked': a shadowed key of the same state is untouched

cases.name: r3_deniedAtConnect_marksRevoked
cases.readme: 'revoked': `connected.deniedEvents` names a subscribed state — keyless, or keyed on the key the connection carries | 'revoked', value kept

cases.name: r4_deniedAtConnect_leavesShadowedKey
cases.readme: 'revoked': A shadowed key of the same state is untouched

cases.name: r5_snapshotOmission_marksRevoked
cases.readme: 'revoked': a snapshot that omits a subscribed state — keyless, or keyed with its key in the query | 'revoked', value kept if one exists

cases.name: r6_snapshotOmission_keyNotInQuery_notMarked
cases.readme: 'revoked': A keyed state whose key the query did not carry is not marked

cases.name: r7_revokeBeforeValue_isRevokedAlone
cases.readme: 'revoked': the mark is kept … apart from the value, so it holds even when no value has arrived yet; createStateClient: `{ status: 'revoked' }` for a state revoked before any value arrived

cases.name: r8_sameConnectionFrame_suppliesValue_staysRevoked
cases.readme: 'revoked': a frame, a read or a snapshot started before the revoke | supplies its value under the ordering rule; the status stays 'revoked'

cases.name: r9_olderFrameOnRevoked_isDropped_markKept
cases.readme: 'revoked': supplies its value under the ordering rule; the status stays 'revoked'; Ordering: older than the stamp | dropped

cases.name: r10_granted_clearsAndReadsOnce_eitherOrder
cases.readme: 'revoked': `subscription.granted` for it | clears the mark for the carried key and reads it once (`get`); the server also sends a frame, before or after the control frame. Both arrive 'ready', and either order ends at the latest value

cases.name: r11_newerConnectionFrame_clearsMark
cases.readme: 'revoked': a frame — the initial one included — … of a connection opened after the revoke, holding the state | clears the mark

cases.name: r12_newerConnectionSnapshot_clearsMark
cases.readme: 'revoked': or the snapshot of a connection opened after the revoke

cases.name: r13_newerConnectionShadowRead_clearsMark
cases.readme: 'revoked': the read of a shadowed key when a connection opened after the revoke, answered | clears the mark the same way

cases.name: r14_olderShadowAnswer_dropsValue_liftsMark
cases.readme: 'revoked': an answer of such a read older than the stamp … its value is dropped under the ordering rule, while the mark is still lifted: the lift goes by the connection, not by `at`

cases.name: r15_snapshotAcrossGrant_omissionNotMarked
cases.readme: 'revoked': Every automatic read is tagged with the connection it was started for, which is how a snapshot in flight across a revoke is told from one read after it

cases.name: r16_snapshotOfOlderConnection_omissionNotMarked
cases.readme: 'revoked': Every automatic read is tagged with the connection it was started for

cases.name: c1_startValue_isReconnectingZero
cases.readme: Connection status: Start value `{ status: 'reconnecting', attempt: 0 }`, a client built with `initial` too

cases.name: c2_nothingSubscribed_isReconnectingZero
cases.readme: Connection status: no stream open — not yet, or nothing subscribed

cases.name: c3_streamOpen_isConnected
cases.readme: Connection status: a stream is open (the SSE `onOpen`)

cases.name: c4_streamRetrying_isReconnectingN
cases.readme: Connection status: the SSE client retrying a dropped one: `attempt` is its count (`onReconnect`)

cases.name: c5_streamConnecting_keepsStatus
cases.readme: Connection status: the SSE client retrying a dropped one: `attempt` is its count

cases.name: c6_streamOffline_isReconnectingN
cases.readme: Connection status: the SSE client retrying a dropped one (offline is a retry, §2-9)

cases.name: c7_streamIdle_isReconnectingZero
cases.readme: Connection status: no stream open — not yet

cases.name: c8_streamClosed_isFailed
cases.readme: Connection status: the retries are exhausted

cases.name: c13_retryWithManifest_reconnectsNow
cases.readme: createStateClient `retry()`: once the manifest is known, reopens the stream now; Connection status: The status is 'reconnecting' 0 until it opens

cases.name: c14_retryWhenConnectedOrUnsubscribed_isNoOp
cases.readme: createStateClient `retry()`: A no-op when 'connected' … and with nothing subscribed

cases.name: c15_keyReopenWhileConnected_staysConnected
cases.readme: Connection status: a reopen on a key change while connected stays 'connected'

cases.name: c16_subscribeWhileFailed_reconnectsSameQuery
cases.readme: Connection status: a `subscribe` restarts when 'failed', reopening a failed stream even when the query is unchanged

cases.name: c17_unsubscribeLeavingOthers_staysFailed
cases.readme: Connection status: An unsubscribe that leaves subscribers never does: the status stays 'failed'

cases.name: c18_lastUnsubscribe_resetsStatusQueryAndCount
cases.readme: Connection status: The last unsubscribe closes the stream: 'reconnecting' 0, the start value, and the first snapshot's retry count starts over for the next wait

cases.name: c21_leavingOfflineWithManifest_doesNothing
cases.readme: Connection status: `retry()` and the browser's `online` event … restart when 'failed' or 'reconnecting' (the stream reopens itself, E-35)

cases.name: c22_subscribeConnection_yieldsCurrentFirst
cases.readme: createStateClient `subscribeConnection`: called with the new status on every change, after `connection()` returns it

cases.name: c23_sameStatus_isNotRepeated
cases.readme: createStateClient `connection()`: the same reference until it changes

cases.name: c24_unavailableStateEvent_reportedOnce_rereadEachOpen
cases.readme: The stream: The client reads the snapshot only when a state it requested is neither in `initial` nor in `deniedEvents`

cases.name: c25_overflow_rereadsSnapshotAndShadows
cases.readme: The stream: A frame sent while no stream was open is lost … The server covers that gap

cases.name: c26_openedAllServed_noSnapshot
cases.readme: The stream: The client reads the snapshot only when a state it requested is neither in `initial` nor in `deniedEvents`

cases.name: c27_openedUnserved_readsSnapshotOnce
cases.readme: The stream: The client reads the snapshot only when a state it requested is neither in `initial` nor in `deniedEvents` (a state whose read threw on the server)

cases.name: c28_openedWithoutInitial_readsSnapshot
cases.readme: The stream: — or when `initial` is absent (a server before it)

cases.name: i1_initial_answersAtOnce
cases.readme: createStateClient: The client installs its manifest and applies each state it holds at construction, keyed states under the query's key, so `current()` answers at once

cases.name: i2_initialOmission_isLoadingNotRevoked
cases.readme: createStateClient: Nothing is marked 'revoked' from it: an omission in the render's snapshot is not a denial by the stream

cases.name: i3_initialKeyedWithoutQueryKey_isSkipped
cases.readme: createStateClient: keyed states under the query's key

cases.name: i4_initial_firstSubscribe_readsNoSnapshot
cases.readme: createStateClient: the first `subscribe` opens the stream without reading the snapshot first; Connection status: a client built with `initial` too: its entries are ready, its stream is not

cases.name: i5_initial_thenFirstFrame_ordersByAt
cases.readme: useServerState: the stream's initial frames bring anything newer; Ordering (O-3)

cases.name: i6_initialStateOutsideManifest_isSkipped
cases.readme: client.ts applyPresent: A state the manifest does not describe … is skipped

cases.name: i7_initial_refusedSubscribe_reportedAtOnce
cases.readme: The manifest: Such a client knows it from construction: nothing above waits, a refused `subscribe` goes to `onError` at once

cases.name: i8_noInitial_firstSubscribe_readsSnapshotFirst
cases.readme: The manifest: The first `subscribe` — or `get`, `write`, `snapshot` — therefore reads the snapshot first: the client installs its manifest, then applies its states, then opens the stream

cases.name: i11_writeOnReadOnlyState_refusedBeforeRequest
cases.readme: The manifest: A `write` on a state the manifest marks `write: false` rejects naming the state, before any request

cases.name: w1_firstSubject_isBaseline_clearsNothing
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D1: the first signed-in value is the baseline; nothing is cleared

cases.name: w2_signedOut_subscriptionIsLoading
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D1, D2, D6: sign-out clears every cell; open subscriptions get loading; reconnecting 0

cases.name: w3_signedOutWhileRevoked_markIsGone
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D2: the revoked mark goes with the value; the next account's read is ready

cases.name: w4_signedInChanged_subscribeIsLoading
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 (Steps): after sign-out and another sign-in, subscribing the same state is loading first

cases.name: w5_directSwitch_subscriptionIsLoading
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D1: another id without nil between clears too (E-43 never passes idle)

cases.name: w6_frameBeforeNewConnection_isDropped
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D4: frames are dropped until an opened of the new id's connection

cases.name: w7_openedForPreviousAccount_isDropped
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D4, D6: an opened whose clientID is the previous account's opens nothing and reads nothing

cases.name: w8_openedForNewAccount_acceptsItsFrames
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D4, D6: the new id's opened is taken as today (C-26 … C-28); then connected

cases.name: w9_snapshotOfPreviousAccount_isNotApplied
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: an automatic read sent for the previous account applies nothing and reports nothing

cases.name: w10_shadowReadOfPreviousAccount_isNotApplied
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: a shadow read sent for the previous account applies nothing

cases.name: w11_getInFlight_refusedSignedInChanged
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: an app get in flight is refused signedInChanged; its answer is not applied

cases.name: w12_writeInFlight_refusedSignedInChanged
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: an app write in flight is refused signedInChanged; its answer is not applied

cases.name: w13_getWaitingOnManifest_refusedAtOnce
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: a call waiting on the manifest is refused at once and never sent

cases.name: w14_snapshotCallInFlight_refusedSignedInChanged
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D3: an app snapshot() in flight is refused signedInChanged; its answer is not applied

cases.name: w15_newAccountsOlderAt_isApplied
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D2: the ordering stamps go too, so the next account's older `at` is applied

cases.name: w16_grantOrRevokeBeforeNewConnection_isDropped
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D4: grant and revoke signals are dropped until an opened of the new id's connection

cases.name: w17_sameSubjectAgain_changesNothing
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D1: a rotation keeps the client id and clears nothing

cases.name: w18_closedClient_stillClears
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D1, D2: a closed client (C-19) keeps its entries, and a change clears them

cases.name: w19_getAfterChange_usesKeptManifest
cases.source: issue #104; state-client-design.md §2-14 D2: the manifest is server-wide and kept; a get after the change reads no snapshot
